design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (professional_email_seats, env_0076). frozen_time 2026-10-24 10:40:00 CDT. Round 12.

[Step 0 — draw and scope]
draw_counts.py --task 1 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 4]}. Round 12 (coordinator route): the annual conversion carries the published annual-start rule (term start date when today is fewer than conversion_start_days 5 days into the paid month, crediting the whole month; term end date when conversion_end_days 3 or fewer days remain, crediting nothing; otherwise today, crediting the days left), the credit days becoming the convention (day by day / whole weeks / none): five factors, the draw met. Round 11 (coordinator route): the late term renewal now carries the renewal product (Harborline Mail Starter scheduled for it) beside the account tier, the price column, the late-payment fee and the seat basis (5). The seat catch-up carries four (tier, price column of the plan, seat basis, billing span) and the annual conversion four (tier, credit fraction, paid-month value, fees carried); that shortfall of one is closed in round 12. Candidates tried for it: (b) a 168-hour cancellation-window refund in place of the catch-up — the subscription is month to month and a month-to-month charge is never refunded (monthly_plan_refundable false), and moving the world to an annual or Microsoft 365 term removes the price-column factor (and, for Microsoft 365, the account tier) from the renewal; the renewal product in the conversion — vacuous, because the late renewal applies the scheduled product and clears it first; the renewal product in the catch-up — the catch-up bills the ended term, whose product is the current one.
Claimed: email_ext_unbilled_seat_catch_up (agent), email_ext_term_renewal (agent), email_ext_annual_conversion (user, PayPal checkout, owner ruling (b)).

[Design thesis]
Surface goal: yearly billing now, however the start date works out; the customer passes the reference number, the amount and the annual start date the agent gives her. Chain: "The annual conversion charge is fixed only after a paid monthly renewal opens a month that runs past today." and "A late renewal is not collected until the charges of the current term carry at least the seats it renews." The renewal due 2026-10-20 was declined three times; it will renew 21 seats (the lower of the scheduled count 21 set on 2026-10-03 and the seat count, never fewer than the 21 mailboxes in use) on Harborline Mail Starter, the product scheduled for it while the month's charges carry only the 15 seats of its opening line, because 8 seats added in October were never billed. So: catch-up (6 seats, up to the scheduled count, the whole ended term) -> late term renewal (21 Starter seats, late-payment fee for 4 days) -> conversion (the annual term starts on the paid month's start 2026-10-20, 4 days back, so all 31 days are credited, its late fee excluded).

[Problem-tree card]
root email_ext_annual_conversion <- email_ext_term_renewal (value_input, gate conversion_credit) <- email_ext_unbilled_seat_catch_up (state_gate, gate email_charges.seats). Sentences verbatim, four-point tests passed. Why false: term 2026-09-20..2026-10-20 ended with declines dfe41329-cc56-4f33-9f5b-75b6f1556ac8, dce74a01-3a42-4da2-90b0-97e07c644db7, 6a11b60d-aeac-4600-a728-5ffef6d14479; 15 seats charged vs 21 renewed. Order unique: run after the renewal, the catch-up reads the new term (21 seats charged, seat count 21, no scheduled count) and bills nothing. Skipped effects: the conversion without the renewal 1046.18; the renewal without the catch-up unchanged in amount (state gate), the 28.44 line missing. No user hint; tools block nothing.

[Base-invariant card]
Step 8: seat_change_active, change_active, m365_cap (not Microsoft 365). Step 10: chargeable_status (active, day 4 of the 7 grace days). Step 12: chargeable_status (active). Overwrites restate base text verbatim for what they do not price (seat-addition clause; mailbox clause; renewal seat-price clause; the conversion's monthly-renewal and month-to-month refund clauses).

[Factor cards]
Catch-up (4), expected 28.44, all-baseline 0.00: tier Bronze 5 (baseline 0 -> 29.94); plan price seat_price_monthly (baseline the annual-commitment price -> 22.74); seat basis (method; multi-source: scheduled count AND idle seats) the lower of 21 and 23, never fewer than 21 in use = 21 (baseline the seat count 23 -> 37.92); billing span (method, date) the term ended with its renewal due -> whole term (baseline the base proration from today, nothing left -> 0.00). RND(6 x 4.99 x 0.95) = 28.44.
Term renewal (5), expected 59.68, all-baseline 91.77: tier (-> 62.29); price column month-to-month (baseline annual-commitment -> 49.70); renewal product Starter scheduled (baseline the current product Plus -> 109.55); late-payment fee 4 days -> late_fee_mid 10.00 (baseline 0 -> 49.68); seat basis 21 (baseline 23 -> 64.41). RND(21 x 2.49 x 0.95) = 49.68 + 10.00 = 59.68.
Conversion (5), expected 426.73, all-baseline 501.48: tier (-> 451.80); credit convention day by day, 27 days left >= 15 (baseline none -> 476.41); annual start the paid month's start, 4 < 5 days in, 31 days credited (baseline today, 27 days -> 433.14); paid month 59.68 (baseline Starter's seat_price_monthly x 21 -> 434.12); fees carried late_fee_mid 10.00 (baseline 0 -> 416.73). RND(21 x 1.99 x 12 x 0.95) = 476.41; credit RND(49.68 x 31/31) = 49.68; 426.73.

[Honest baselines (CG-10 class)]
No tier (Business accounts), the annual-commitment seat price (annual_prepaid subscribers), the seat count as catch-up target and renewed seats (no schedule, no idle seat), the base proration of added seats, no late fee (a renewal paid on its due date), no credit convention (a conversion on the month's last day), the annual term starting on the conversion day with the days left credited (a conversion mid-month), the paid month at list, no fee carried.

[Factor-reads table (XF A1, r8/mech.py)]
both seat-basis factors read scheduled_seats / seat_count_now (plain); paid month reads converted_seats (plain); the rest read records only.

[All-pairs method tiers (XF A6)]
seat basis (catch-up target and renewed seats): MX(seat - idle, MN(scheduled, seat)) | seat - idle | seat. catch-up span: 1 | whole weeks x 7 / term days | days / term days. credit convention: credited days / month | whole weeks x 7 / month | 0. annual start (parameter): term start, whole month | term end, nothing | today, days left. paid month: opening amount | opening + added-seat amounts | seat_price_monthly x seats.

[Probes (XF B9/B10, r8t/probes.py)]
Another customer's account never matches; absent account -> no rate. A prior-term renewal or an added-seat line of another period never matches the opening-charge reads; no opening charge -> every seat counts as unbilled, the paid month falls to list, no fee. Late days 0 -> no fee; fee days negative -> no fee. The idle window uses the stated whole-month test.

[Events and triggers (XF D20); owed at once (XF D21)]
Catch-up email_seat_charge added_seats, card; renewal email_renewal_charge -> email_term_renew, card; conversion email_renewal_charge, paypal. Nothing lands in another category. Nothing else falls due before 2026-10-27; the credit balance is 0.00 since the 2026-09-30 withdrawal, so no charge can be paid from credit.

[Seed rows]
customers (K=2), account Bronze + ledger (500.00 deposit, six credit-first payments of 71.11, 73.34 withdrawn on 2026-09-30, balance 0.00, so each October attempt, a 49.68 term renewal by the published rules, went to the card), email holding (Plus monthly, 23 seats, scheduled 21), charges (order 74.85, March renewal 74.85, April-September 71.11, each a term renewal paid on time), events (pat@ 2026-09-22, lee@ 2026-10-09, jo@ 2026-10-12 restored 2026-10-14, three declines).

[Persona design]
Rosa volunteers only the yearly switch; passive replies on identity, the October seats and the scheduled drop to 21, the deletions, the replacement card, account credit (no); pays the yearly charge herself with the company PayPal at checkout.

[Verification]
r8t/t1.py with each prior write applied; no rounded input within 1e-6 of a half cent.

[Revision log]
r1-r5 rate card, owner ruling, included seats; r6 bands and plan factors; r7 honest rebuild below the draw; r8: plan price, three-band late-payment fee, scheduled target, world re-seeded (scheduled count 21, pat@ deleted 2026-09-22); r9: kept seats removed, one seat-basis method, catch-up billing span; r11: renewal product and price column in the term renewal, Starter scheduled on the world; r12: annual-start factor in the conversion, credit days as the convention, world unchanged; r13: the annual start date is an argument the agent supplies to the conversion checkout; scoped overwrite of the email_plan_changes storage skip for the term renewal; the renewal product is an argument the agent supplies to the renewal tool, and an upgrade line of the current term keeps the current product (the record test that decides when a scheduled product applies). r14: the persona hands over the annual start date the agent gives and has no start-date preference of her own. r16 (this): seed realism: the unused credit is withdrawn before the October attempts, so the credit-first auto-renew finds 0.00 and the card is declined.
user_scenario:
You are Rosa Paredes, who owns Prairie Signal IT LLC, a small IT support company in Dallas. Your company's own mailboxes on prairiesignal.com run on Harborline Mail, paid month to month, and you have decided it is time to put them on yearly billing now, however the start date works out, because paying every month has become a nuisance. That switch is the only thing you are calling about. You are brisk and practical, you like to hear the plan and the numbers before anything happens, and you don't pretend to know Harborline's billing rules.

When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Rosa Paredes. To confirm the account you give your phone number, 4695550157, and your support PIN, 452617; only if they need more do you add that your card ends in 4682 and your billing ZIP is 75208. You don't remember reference numbers, amounts or dates. If asked about seats, you say you added eight people at the start of October and then set the subscription to drop to 21 seats at the next renewal, because two of them were only temporary; one person left in late September and another in early October and you deleted their mailboxes, and one mailbox you deleted by mistake in October was put back two days later; beyond that, go by what the account shows.

You are fine with the agent sorting out anything on the account that has to be dealt with to get you onto yearly billing, as long as they explain what it is and what it costs first; once they have, you tell them to go ahead. If the agent mentions that the mail was set to move down to Mail Starter at the renewal, you confirm you set that in early October, since Starter is all the staff need, and you want the yearly billing on Starter. If the agent tells you this month's renewal didn't go through, you explain that your bank replaced your card in October after a fraud scare and the new card ending 4682 is on the account now, so they can charge small monthly items like that to it; you don't want to use the account credit. The yearly payment itself you want to make yourself from the company's PayPal, because your bookkeeper wants every annual purchase on that PayPal account, and that PayPal account is not saved on your Harborline account; so when the agent hands you the yearly checkout, you complete it yourself for the prairiesignal.com subscription with the reference number, the amount and the annual start date the agent gives you. Once the agent confirms the mail is on yearly billing, you thank them and end the chat.

edges.condition: email_charges carries a renewal charge whose period start is email_holdings.term_start_date, and email_holdings.term_end_date is later than today's date while the status is active.
edges.policy_source: The annual conversion charge is fixed only after a paid monthly renewal opens a month that runs past today.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-10-24 the month on record ended on 2026-10-20 and its renewal was declined three times; no renewal charge opens a month that runs past today.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The late renewal books a renewal line opening 2026-10-20, charged 2026-10-24, and moves the term to 2026-10-20..2026-11-20 with 21 seats on Harborline Mail Starter; the conversion then reads 21 Starter seats, the opening line's 59.68 amount, its 10.00 late fee and a paid month begun 4 days before today.

edges.condition: The seats on the charge that opened the current term plus the seats on added-seat lines whose period end is the term end date are at least the renewed seats: where a scheduled seat count is set, the lower of it and the seat count but never fewer than the seat count less the idle seats of the current term; otherwise the seat count less those idle seats.
edges.policy_source: A late renewal is not collected until the charges of the current term carry at least the seats it renews.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The term's charges carry 15 seats (the opening renewal line, no added-seat line ending 2026-10-20), while the renewal will renew 21 seats (the scheduled seat count 21, which equals the mailboxes in use).
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The seat catch-up books an added-seat line of 6 seats for 2026-09-20..2026-10-20, so the term's charges carry 21 seats, the seats the renewal renews, and it may be collected.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A chain: the conversion waits on the late renewal, which waits on the seat catch-up. The order is also forced by the records: run after the renewal, the catch-up would read the new term (21 seats on its opening line, seat count 21, no scheduled count) and bill nothing (actual run: 0.00), so only catch-up -> renewal -> conversion is a topological order and it is the one the prerequisite sentences state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the late term renewal and replaying the conversion on the post-catch-up world gives conversion_amount 1046.18 instead of 426.73 (23 seats at seat_price_annual_prepaid, no credit because the month on record ended four days ago); no renewal line is booked.

Skipping the seat catch-up leaves the 6 unbilled seats with no billing line (terminal email_charges lacks the 28.44 added-seat line) and the renewal is collected while the term's charges still carry only 15 of the 21 seats it renews; renewal_amount itself stays 59.68, the edge is a state gate.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to switch prairiesignal.com mail to yearly billing; it never mentions unbilled seats, the declined October renewal or any payment, and the card replacement is told only after the agent says the renewal did not go through.
